reproduction_target: The computational half of the study: re-derivation, from the raw paired-end Illumina shotgun reads, of (i) the CZID/IDseq taxonomic abundance tables per sample, (ii) the CZID AMR (CARD-based) resistome table underlying Table 1 / Table 2 and the reported read counts (tet(C) 70,049 reads; APH(3')-Ia 4,498 reads), and (iii) the R-side statistics and figures: Shannon/richness alpha diversity with the reported test statistics (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.000416 by sample type, p = 0.042 by location), Bray-Curtis NMDS ordination, and PERMANOVA (adonis2) effect sizes (sample type R2 = 0.645, p = 0.001; location R2 = 0.068, p = 0.937), plus the top-20 taxa / top-20 Vibrio / Vibrio-linked AMR panels (Fig. 4, Fig. 5). Wet-lab field sampling, DNA extraction and sequencing are out of scope (OOS).
granularity_note: The Methods section (2.1 Site Description and Sample Processing, 2.2 Nucleic Acid Extractions and Processing, 2.3 Bioinformatics and Statistical Analysis) is 3 short subsections; 2.3 - the entire computational description - is a single paragraph of roughly 180 words. The computational step list below is therefore reconstructed at the level of 'named analysis' rather than 'invocation', because no invocation-level detail exists anywhere in the paper. Step C7 (BLAST of detected Vibrio phages) is not in the Methods at all; it is reported only in the Discussion ('BLAST analysis of the recorded phages was inconclusive, returning no clear integrase or lysis annotations') and is included because it is a named computational analysis whose result is used in the paper's argument. Steps C5 and C6 are separated because the prose describes two distinct curation passes over the CZID output (Fig. 4 panels vs Fig. 5). Figure 3 (AMR long-tail) is produced by the same C2/C5 path and is not given its own step. There is no supplementary material and no methods citation chain that supplies parameters: the one methods reference, Cyphert et al. 2024 (doi:10.1101/2024.05.15.594453), is cited for the wet-lab DNA extraction and for the statistical framing, not for a code artifact.

steps.label: Field sampling, November 2023, at five San Francisco Bay sites (Loch Lomond, Point San Quentin, Brickyard Park, China Camp, Dunphy Park): sediment from the upper 10 cm into three 50 mL Falcon tubes; biofilm scrapes into three 15 mL Falcon tubes prefilled with 99.5% ethanol; oysters (>=5 individuals per site) into sterilized bags; transport on ice, storage at -80 C

DNA extraction following Cyphert et al. 2024: oyster tissue 25 mg +/- 1 mg incubated at 56 C overnight (12+ hrs); sediment and biofilm via DNeasy PowerSoil Pro Kit per manufacturer instructions; extracted DNA stored at -80 C
Paired-end Illumina shotgun metagenomic sequencing at 30-50M read depth (instrument model, read length, library kit and sequencing provider are not stated)

CZID (formerly IDseq) Illumina mNGS pipeline run on the raw FASTQ: host filtering, quality control, alignment and taxonomic classification, returning per-sample microbial abundance tables (verbatim: 'Raw sequencing data was processed using CZID's illumina pipeline, an open-source, cloud-based pipeline for metagenomic analysis (Kalantar et al., 2020). CZID performs host filtering, quality control, alignment, and taxonomic classification services, returning microbial abundance tables for each sample.')

CZID AMR module run on the same samples to produce the resistome profile (verbatim: 'AMR data was also processed through the CZID pipeline (Alcock et al., 2019).'), i.e. CARD-based resistance gene detection yielding the read counts in Table 1 and Table 2

Alpha diversity in RStudio: Shannon index and richness computed per sample and tested across sample type and location (Methods say 'a one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) that yielded significance across sample type and location'; the figure legends and Results instead report Kruskal-Wallis, p = 0.000416 by sample type and p = 0.042 by location - the two statements disagree about which test was run)

Beta diversity in RStudio: genus-level Bray-Curtis dissimilarity, NMDS ordination (Fig. 2A/2B) and PERMANOVA via the adonis2 function, testing sample type and location (reported: sample type R2 = 0.645, p = 0.001; location R2 = 0.068, p = 0.937). The package providing adonis2 (vegan) is never named, the permutation count is never given, and no random seed is stated for either the NMDS starts or the permutation test

Curation and plotting in R of the CZID output into the Fig. 4 panels (verbatim: 'CZID raw NTR data and associated sample metadata was organized into the following categories: Top 20 Taxa by site (Fig4A), and by sample type (Fig4B) using R. Similarly, top 20 Vibrio and known AMR sequence data was also sorted by site (Fig4C) and sample type (Fig4D) using R software.'). No normalization, rarefaction, NT/NR score threshold, or background-model filter is stated for the 'raw NTR data'

Extraction and sorting in R of Vibrio-associated AMR sequences from the oyster microbiomes to produce Fig. 5 / Table 2 (verbatim: 'Finally, these curated data sets were used to pull out and sort Vibrio associated AMR sequences from the oyster microbiomes using R statistical analysis as well (Fig5).'). The rule by which an AMR hit is declared 'Vibrio associated' - e.g. contig co-assignment, read-level taxonomic call, or CARD organism annotation - is never defined

BLAST search of the detected Vibrio phage sequences to determine lifestyle (reported only in the Discussion: 'BLAST analysis of the recorded phages was inconclusive regarding lifestyle, returning no clear integrase or lysis annotations'). No BLAST program, database, version, e-value or identity threshold is given, and the query sequences are not deposited

headline.static_readiness: 0/7 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 0/7 (0%). Not one computational step reaches RI even under the most generous inference-inclusive reading, and the binding constraint is the data axis rather than the code axis. The paper carries no Data Availability statement and no Code Availability statement of any kind - the article body consists only of Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Implications for Monitoring and Management, and References - and a case-insensitive scan of the JATS full text and of the bioRxiv v1 landing page for accession/BioProject/PRJNA/PRJEB/SRA/ENA/GEO/figshare/Zenodo/Dryad/GitHub/GitLab/supplementary returns zero matches. The raw shotgun reads are therefore not obtainable, so every C-step scores data = 0 and nothing can rise above NI. The four NI steps (C1-C4) are those where the analysis is at least performed by a named, publicly documented instrument - the CZID/IDseq cloud pipeline for C1/C2, standard named statistics (Shannon, Bray-Curtis, adonis2) for C3/C4 - so a reader with the reads could plausibly re-run them; the three X steps (C5-C7) are bespoke R curation and an ad-hoc BLAST whose selection rules and parameters are not merely unpinned but undefined, so they are under-determined even with author-supplied data. Per the symmetric-qualifier rule this zero under-claims by construction: Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present artifact, and it remains possible that a CZID project exists and is shareable. Stage 2 cannot lift this paper, because there is no source artifact for stage 2 to read.
headline.coverage: 7 computational steps assessed against 3 wet-lab steps; computational coverage 7/10 = 70% of the reconstructed step list, |S| = 7, |W| = 3. Coverage of the true pipeline is necessarily partial and is a floor, not a census: section 2.3 is a single ~180-word paragraph that names platforms and statistics but no invocations, so intermediate operations that certainly occurred (host-genome selection for CZID filtering, NT/NR score thresholding, count normalization before ordination, the taxon-level aggregation to genus) are invisible and are folded into the steps above rather than counted separately. Sample sizes per matrix and per site are never stated in the paper, so the number of libraries behind each step is also unknown.

repro_index.coverage: 7/10 steps computational (|S| = 7, |W| = 3); prose-only stage-1 read of a single-paragraph Methods subsection

gaps.where: All seven computational steps (C1-C7); the paper as a whole
gaps.missing: No analysis code is deposited or linked. The paper contains no Code Availability statement; its sections are Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Implications for Monitoring and Management, and References only. A case-insensitive scan of the JATS XML full text and of the bioRxiv v1 landing page for github / gitlab / bitbucket / zenodo / softwareheritage / osf / codeocean returns zero matches. The R work is described only as 'Statistical analyses were performed using RStudio (RStudio 2021)' and as things done 'using R' / 'using R software' / 'using R statistical analysis as well'; no script, notebook, or supplementary code file is named or attached. No repository was searched for on the open web, per protocol.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the R analysis scripts (import of the CZID NT/NR tables, filtering and normalization, alpha/beta diversity, adonis2 call, and the top-20 / Vibrio-AMR curation) as a tagged repository release archived to a Zenodo DOI, and cite that DOI in a Code Availability statement.

gaps.where: Input to C1/C2; the sample-to-library correspondence for every downstream step
gaps.missing: No sequence data deposit and no sample manifest. No BioProject, SRA/ENA run accession, GEO series, figshare or Zenodo record, and no CZID project identifier or public-project link appears anywhere in the paper or on the landing page. The paper also never states how many libraries were sequenced, how many per matrix (oyster tissue / biofilm / sediment / water), or how many per site; the water matrix is analysed throughout but is not described in section 2.1's field-collection protocol at all, which lists only sediment, biofilm and oysters. The 'associated sample metadata' referred to in section 2.3 is not provided, so even the mapping from FASTQ to site and matrix is unavailable.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the raw paired-end FASTQ under a BioProject with per-run SRA/ENA accessions, publish a sample sheet mapping each run to site, matrix, collection date and replicate, and additionally share the CZID project as a public project so the exact platform-side inputs and outputs are inspectable.

gaps.where: Software environment for every computational step (C1-C7)
gaps.missing: No version pin of any kind, i.e. gap subtype 2a (version not stated) rather than 2b (floating lower bound). The CZID/IDseq pipeline version and workflow release are not given - CZID is cited only bibliographically as Kalantar et al. 2020, and the paper does not even state which CZID pipeline version or host-filtering reference was used, although the Discussion acknowledges that host-genome choice materially affected the result ('high host read proportions on this type of oyster (O. edulis genomes) can inflate apparent host signal in metagenomic classifications such as CZID'). On the R side, 'RStudio (RStudio 2021)' names an IDE and a year, not an R version; no package versions are given, and vegan (which supplies adonis2) is not even named. There is no conda environment, no lockfile, no renv.lock, no requirements file, and no container image or digest.
gaps.how_to_close: State the CZID pipeline version and workflow release used for both the mNGS and the AMR runs, and ship an renv.lock or a container digest for the R analysis together with the R version and the CRAN/Bioconductor snapshot date.

gaps.where: C1 (CZID host filtering and taxonomic classification reference) and C2 (CZID AMR reference database)
gaps.missing: Both reference resources are consumed out of band and unpinned in the prose. For C1 the host genome or host-index used for filtering is not named (this matters: the paper's own Discussion attributes the unexpected Ostrea edulis signal to host-genome behaviour), and the NCBI nt/nr index version behind CZID's alignment and taxonomic call is not stated. For C2 the AMR reference is identified only by citing Alcock et al. 2019 - i.e. CARD - with no CARD version or release date, no CARD-RGI version, and no detection thresholds. CZID's reference indices are updated over time, so the same submission today would not consult the same database. Stage-1 is prose-only, so no env_capture_class (A/B/C) is assigned here; this is recorded as a prose-visible unpinned-reference gap for a stage-2 code check that cannot happen because there is no code.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the CZID pipeline/index version stamped on the run and the CARD release version (or the versioned DOI of the AMR database snapshot), and report them alongside the abundance tables so a reanalysis can pin the same references.

gaps.missing: The bespoke selection logic is neither published nor described well enough to reconstruct. For C5, the input is called 'CZID raw NTR data' with no NT/NR score threshold, no read-count or rPM cutoff, no background-model / negative-control subtraction, no rarefaction or normalization, and no statement of whether host-assigned reads were removed before computing 'top 20'. For C6, the rule that makes an AMR hit 'Vibrio associated' is never defined - contig co-assembly, read-level taxonomy, or CARD's own organism annotation would give different answers, and this rule is what produces the paper's headline claim that oyster tissue uniquely harbours Vibrio cholerae varG. For C7, no BLAST program, database, version, e-value or identity threshold is given and the phage query sequences are not deposited, so the 'inconclusive' lifestyle result is not checkable. No negative or extraction-blank controls are reported anywhere, despite section 5 recommending exactly that practice to others.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the curation scripts with the explicit thresholds, and state the taxonomic-attribution rule used for Vibrio-linked AMR calls together with the control samples used to filter contamination.

gaps.where: C4 (NMDS ordination and adonis2 permutation test)
gaps.missing: Both procedures are stochastic and no seed is reported. NMDS uses random starting configurations and adonis2 computes its p-value from a permutation distribution; the number of permutations is not stated (the reported p = 0.001 is consistent with the vegan default of 999 permutations, but this is an inference, not a statement), no seed is set, and no convergence or stress value is reported for the NMDS. Exact reproduction of the ordination coordinates and of the p-value to the last digit is therefore not expected; only distributional agreement could be checked.
gaps.how_to_close: Set and report a random seed, state the permutation count, and report the NMDS stress and number of random starts alongside the ordination.

gaps.where: C1 and C2 - the entire upstream half of the analysis
gaps.missing: The primary metagenomic processing is externalized to a hosted third-party service (CZID, formerly IDseq) rather than executed locally. The pipeline is genuinely open source, which is why C1 and C2 score code = 1 rather than 0, but the paper pins nothing about the instance: no project link, no pipeline version, no run identifier, no parameter set, and no export of the intermediate NT/NR tables. Reproduction therefore depends on the continued availability and behavioural stability of an external service and cannot be pinned from the paper alone.
gaps.how_to_close: Export and deposit the CZID sample reports (NT/NR tables and the AMR report) as static supplementary files with the pipeline version stamped, and share the CZID project publicly, so the downstream R analysis is reproducible even if the service changes.

gaps.missing: Field collection, DNA extraction and Illumina sequencing are wet-lab steps and are excluded from the computational denominator (|S| = 7 of 10 reconstructed steps). Recorded here for completeness only, not as a penalty. Note in passing that the wet-lab description is itself incomplete on a point that affects the computational side: water sampling is never described in section 2.1 although water is one of the four analysed matrices, and the sequencing description gives only 'paired-end illumina shotgun sequencing (30-50M read depth)' with no instrument, read length or library preparation kit.
gaps.how_to_close: Not applicable to the computational readiness score. For completeness the authors could state the water-collection protocol, the instrument and read length, and the library kit.
